title: A seven-metabolite AI model detected renal-cell carcinoma across six validation cohorts
summary: An SVM-based screen of untargeted plasma metabolomics identified candidate renal-cell-carcinoma metabolites, which were confirmed by targeted analysis and used in the RCAID AI diagnostic model. In 1,680 participants across five hospitals, seven plasma metabolites supported AUROCs of 0.977, 0.911, 0.945 and 0.972 in internal, external, multicenter and temporal validation cohorts, respectively; validation also included late-stage and non-clear-cell RCC. The authors report six associated dysregulated pathways from multi-omic analyses.
ai_technology: Support-vector-machine metabolite selection and the Renal Cell Carcinoma Artificial Intelligence Detector (RCAID)
organization: Peking University First Hospital and Peking University Health Science Center; Beijing Miyun Hospital; Beijing Friendship Hospital; collaborating Chinese hospitals

evidence.tested: An SVM-based screen of untargeted plasma metabolomics identified candidate renal-cell-carcinoma metabolites, which were confirmed by targeted analysis and used in the RCAID AI diagnostic model.
evidence.unknown: The study used diagnostic case-control cohorts with healthy controls, so reported discrimination does not establish population-screening performance, clinical utility, or improved outcomes. Most cases were clear-cell RCC (81%) and stage I (69%); subtype and cohort composition may affect generalizability. The abstract reports multi-omic pathway associations but does not establish causal mechanisms. Samples were collected 2019–2023; source publication date is the 2025 online-first date. Source checked; independent replication not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: The source states that an SVM was used to identify candidate metabolites from untargeted plasma profiles; targeted metabolomics confirmed selected metabolites. The resulting seven-feature AI-aided RCAID model was evaluated in six independent internal, external, multicenter, temporal, late-stage and non-clear-cell validation cohorts.
